name: Doris Kowalczyk, Step-Down: hip fracture ORIF, CAUTI, SNF transfer

caseMeta.title: Step-Down Unit: Right hip fracture, ORIF (POD 2), catheter-associated UTI, transfer to a skilled nursing facility (3 shifts)
learningObjectives: Provide safe post-operative care after hip fracture fixation: pain, neurovascular checks, mobility, VTE prevention, incision care and fall prevention.
Recognize early signs of a catheter-associated urinary tract infection, including new confusion in an older adult, and act with SBAR communication.
Use the catheter-associated UTI prevention bundle and ask whether the catheter is still needed every day.
Prepare an older adult for safe transfer to a skilled nursing facility with a complete handoff.

encounter.attending: S. Patel, MD (Hospitalist); A. Reyes, MD (Orthopedic Surgery)
encounter.diagnosis: Right intertrochanteric femur fracture after a fall, status post ORIF with cephalomedullary nail (Sunday 11/08), postoperative day 2
encounter.chiefComplaint: Right hip pain after a fall at home
encounter.dietOrder: Consistent-carbohydrate, 2 g sodium diet with protein supplement
encounter.ambulationOrder: Weight bearing as tolerated, right leg; up with 1 assist and walker

problems.name: Right intertrochanteric femur fracture, status post ORIF with cephalomedullary nail (POD 2)
problems.details: Fall at home Saturday 2130. Surgery Sunday 1430-1615 under spinal anesthesia, blood loss 350 mL. Weight bearing as tolerated. Enoxaparin for 35 days.

problems.name: Postoperative anemia (Hgb 7.9, transfused 1 unit; 9.0 now)
problems.details: Monitor Hgb and for bleeding at the incision.

problems.name: Hypertension, type 2 diabetes (A1c 7.2%), CKD stage 3a, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis
problems.details: Lisinopril and metformin on hold; insulin correction scale; levothyroxine continues.

problems.name: Impaired mobility and high fall risk; discharge to skilled nursing facility
problems.details: Lives alone in a two-story home. SNF rehabilitation planned (Maple Grove).

problems.name: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection (catheter day 4-5)
problems.details: Recognized Tuesday 2100: T 100.8, new confusion, suprapubic discomfort. UA positive 2230, cultures sent 2145, ceftriaxone 1 g IV at 2330, Foley removed 2200.

observations.label: Urine culture (catheter sampling port)
observations.value: Gram-negative rods, more than 100,000 CFU/mL. Identification and susceptibilities to follow.

orders.name: cefazolin (ANCEF) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 2 g IV Every 8 hours x3 doses.
orders.rationale: Surgical prophylaxis for the hip fracture fixation

medication.importantInfo: Stopped after 24 hours; no sulfa or cephalosporin allergy.

orders.name: packed red blood cells (1 unit)
orders.instructions: Administer 1 unit IV Once over 3.5 hours.

orders.name: fentanyl injection
orders.instructions: Administer 25 mcg IV Once.
orders.rationale: Hip fracture pain in the ED

orders.name: lactated Ringer's 1,000 mL
orders.instructions: Administer 75 mL/h IV Continuous until 0900 Tuesday.
orders.rationale: Post-operative maintenance fluid while intake is low

orders.name: oxygen by nasal cannula
orders.instructions: Administer 2 L/min Inhalation Continuous, keep SpO2 92% or higher.

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 1,000 mg Oral Every 8 hours (maximum 3 g per day).
orders.rationale: Multimodal pain control after hip surgery

medication.importantInfo: Acetaminophen lowers fever: record the temperature BEFORE giving it.
medication.hold: Hold for AST/ALT over 3 times normal. Count every acetaminophen dose in 24 hours.

orders.name: enoxaparin (LOVENOX) injection
orders.instructions: Administer 40 mg Subcutaneous Daily at 0900.
orders.rationale: Blood clot prevention after hip fracture surgery (about 35 days)

medication.importantInfo: Rotate abdominal sites, do not expel the air bubble, do not rub.
medication.hold: Hold and call for bleeding, platelets under 100, or creatinine clearance under 30.

orders.name: levothyroxine (SYNTHROID) tablet
orders.frequency: Daily at 0600 on an empty stomach
orders.instructions: Administer 75 mcg Oral Daily at 0600 on an empty stomach.

medication.freqKey: Daily at 0600 on an empty stomach

orders.name: atorvastatin (LIPITOR) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 20 mg Oral Daily at bedtime.

orders.name: calcium carbonate with vitamin D tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 500 mg / 400 units Oral Twice daily with meals.

orders.name: senna-docusate (SENOKOT-S) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 2 tablets Oral Twice daily.

orders.name: polyethylene glycol (MIRALAX) powder
orders.instructions: Administer 17 g Oral Daily.

orders.name: insulin lispro (HUMALOG) correction scale
orders.instructions: Glucose 151-200: 2 units; 201-250: 4 units; 251-300: 6 units; 301-350: 8 units; over 350: 10 units and call. Under 70: hypoglycemia protocol.
orders.rationale: Type 2 diabetes while metformin is held

orders.name: lisinopril (PRINIVIL,ZESTRIL) tablet
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Oral Daily.

medication.importantInfo: Held Sunday and Monday for low blood pressure; resume when BP and creatinine are stable.
medication.hold: Hold for systolic BP under 110, creatinine rising, or potassium over 5.0.

orders.name: ceftriaxone (ROCEPHIN) injection
orders.instructions: Give 1 g IV over 30 minutes after the cultures are drawn. Continue daily; the provider will tailor it to the final urine culture. At the SNF it can be given 1 g IM with lidocaine.
orders.rationale: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection (sulfa allergy: no TMP-SMX; no fluoroquinolone in an 82-year-old with delirium)

medication.importantInfo: No known cephalosporin allergy. Cultures were drawn at 2145 before the first dose.

orders.name: oxycodone (ROXICODONE) tablet
orders.frequency: Every 4 hours as needed (2.5 mg for pain 4-6, 5 mg for pain 7-10)
orders.instructions: Administer 2.5-5 mg Oral Every 4 hours as needed (2.5 mg for pain 4-6, 5 mg for pain 7-10).

medication.importantInfo: Age 82 with a new infection: new confusion is a reason to hold the dose and call.
medication.freqKey: Every 4 hours as needed (2.5 mg for pain 4-6, 5 mg for pain 7-10)
medication.hold: Hold for sedation, RR under 12, or new confusion; call the provider.

orders.name: ondansetron (ZOFRAN) injection
orders.frequency: Every 8 hours as needed for nausea
orders.instructions: Administer 4 mg IV Every 8 hours as needed for nausea.

medication.freqKey: Every 8 hours as needed for nausea

orders.name: bisacodyl (DULCOLAX) suppository
orders.frequency: Daily as needed for no bowel movement in 2 days
orders.instructions: Administer 10 mg Rectal Daily as needed for no bowel movement in 2 days.

medication.freqKey: Daily as needed for no bowel movement in 2 days

orders.name: acetaminophen (TYLENOL) 650 mg PRN fever
orders.frequency: Every 6 hours as needed for temperature over 100.4 F (no more than 3 g in 24 hours total)
orders.instructions: Administer 650 mg Oral Every 6 hours as needed for temperature over 100.4 F (no more than 3 g in 24 hours total).

medication.freqKey: Every 6 hours as needed for temperature over 100.4 F (no more than 3 g in 24 hours total)
medication.hold: Do not give if the scheduled acetaminophen was given in the last 4 hours or the 24-hour total would pass 3 g.

orders.name: Consistent-carbohydrate, 2 g sodium diet with protein supplement twice daily
orders.instructions: Encourage fluids (1,500 mL or more per day unless told otherwise) and protein. Dietitian following.

orders.name: Weight bearing as tolerated, right leg; up with 1 assist and walker with PT/OT and nursing
orders.instructions: No hip precautions for an intramedullary nail. Up to chair for all meals. Fall precautions: bed alarm on, call light in reach, non-skid socks, glasses and left hearing aid on.

orders.name: Neurovascular checks, right leg, every 4 hours
orders.instructions: Check the right foot: pulses (dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial), capillary refill, color, warmth, sensation, toe movement. Call the surgeon for loss of pulse, cool pale foot, numbness or new severe pain. Watch the thigh for swelling.

orders.name: Incision and dressing check; keep the dressing dry and intact
orders.instructions: Aquacel dressing stays on until the follow-up visit unless saturated. Mark and call for drainage over 3 cm.

orders.name: Incentive spirometry every hour while awake; cough and deep breathe

stickyNotes.body: High fall risk: bed alarm on, glasses and left hearing aid in. Any new confusion in an 82-year-old needs a full check (temperature, glucose, oxygen, pain, bladder) and a call.

stickyNotes.body: UA positive at 2230 Tuesday, urine and blood cultures sent 2145 before antibiotics, ceftriaxone 1 g IV given 2330, Foley removed 2200. Sulfa allergy: no TMP-SMX. Watch temperature, mental status and voiding.
